opportunities.title: APEX Awards

amount.raw: Applicants can apply for up to £200,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers at a UK university or UK not-for-profit research organisation, holding a permanent or fixed-term position covering the award duration, with teaching and admin duties that can be relieved. Lead may include up to two Co-applicants covering different Academy remits.
opportunities.summary: Cross-disciplinary 'blue skies' research awards in partnership with the Royal Society, Royal Academy of Engineering and Leverhulme Trust, supporting interdisciplinary research across science, engineering and the social sciences/humanities. Awards up to 24 months.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call, across any career stage. Prior public engagement experience expected. Previous successful recipients not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a GLAM organisation or performing arts organisation. Awards run between 1 April 2027 and 31 December 2028.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career scholars in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', held 21-23 April 2027. Symposium covers travel, accommodation and visa costs, with seed funding available for international collaborations.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: Funded at 80% of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC, for three years

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in humanities/social sciences based at a UK university or recognised research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of doctorate location; any nationality with a UK doctorate eligible. Viva Voce completed between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Must not hold a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three-year fellowship for outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project, completing a significant piece of publishable research. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based HEI or IRO continuing for the full award duration. Lead applicants without a doctorate may have equivalent experience.
opportunities.summary: Awards promoting the acquisition and advancement of skills (quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages) by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination. Awards of 6-12 months.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: Up to £300,000 over 2 years (80% FEC; total project value at 100% FEC up to £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: PI must be a researcher from the humanities or social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute, postdoctoral or above, spending at least 20% time on the award, with overseas Co-Applicants required. Genuine interdisciplinarity across SHAPE/STEM required.
opportunities.summary: Supports genuinely interdisciplinary international research projects led by UK-based humanities/social sciences researchers on the theme of 'Mobilities', covering movement of people, materials and ideas. 24-month awards starting March/April 2027, supported by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers to embed in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, developing skills, networks and careers in policy sectors. Up to two one-year fellowships. Areas: security/defence, Indo-European relations, technology and AI, strategy-making in Europe.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Current British Academy award-holders OR applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award within the next six months who need support with their application.
opportunities.summary: Rolling funding to support additional needs of applicants and award-holders, e.g. equipment to overcome barriers for disabled researchers, assistance for sensory impairment, caring costs for research away from home, and support to make an application. Reviewed monthly.
